findings.title: completeIntent duplicates reviseIntent's particulars-serialisation block verbatim, in the same file
findings.lines: 326-331 (new) vs. 396-400 (pre-existing reviseIntent, unchanged by this diff)
findings.judgement: A labelled judgement call per the smell baseline, not a hard violation -- the ticket's own brief asked for 'following the existing reviseIntent/authorityIntent pattern,' which this satisfies. Extracting a small `serializeParticulars(p: Record<string, unknown>): string` helper both functions call would remove the duplication without changing either intent tuple's shape or any test's expected string. No documented repo standard endorses the duplication, so the baseline is not overridden here.
findings.required_fix: Optional: extract the shared five-line block into one helper (e.g. serializeParticulars) called from both completeIntent and reviseIntent.

findings.title: The disposeIntent test's title claims 'memo EXCLUDED' but memo is excluded structurally (not part of the type at all), so nothing in the test body demonstrates the exclusion at runtime
findings.lines: test named "#978 disposeIntent: one decision while the money facts are unchanged, a new one the moment any of them move — memo EXCLUDED"
findings.evidence: disposeIntent's own parameter type (apps/web/lib/registers/fixed-assets.ts) has no `memo` field at all, so no object literal that includes it can be passed without a TypeScript error (short of an `as any` cast the test does not use). The test asserts four 'a different X yields a different intent' cases (proceeds, date, cost portion, proceeds account) and ends with a code comment explaining the door's own memo-exclusion, but never constructs two calls that differ only by memo and asserts the resulting keys are equal -- because there is no runtime way to do so given the type. The behaviour the title claims to prove is real (confirmed by reading disposeIntent's signature and the door's own 0041:3667-3671 comment), but it is proven by the type system and documented by a comment, not demonstrated by this test's assertions.
findings.judgement: Not a test-quality defect in the /tdd sense (no tautology, no internal-collaborator seam, no mock of something the repo controls) -- it is a naming precision nit: the test name overstates what its own assertions show.
findings.required_fix: Optional: reword the test title to something like '...money facts drive the decision; memo has no field to test because the type excludes it' or drop the 'memo EXCLUDED' clause from the title and leave it to the comment.

summary: Reviewed the STANDARDS axis for riders wave 3, lane 04 (#932, #882, #975, #978 -- fixed assets) against AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, WORK-ORDER.md/RIG.md (including the wave-2 and wave-3 addenda), the /tdd skill, and the house migration law, over git diff ffe63a0dd08...HEAD. All three new migrations (0277/0278/0279) fully satisfy the documented house shape: measured prestate pins (never carried over from an older migration), SECURITY DEFINER/search_path/owner preserved and re-checked in the tail, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY plus zero application-role DML on both new tables, preintegration gates and rig-meta cohorts present and correctly ordered, and independently-recomputed sha256 hashes match the values recorded in the shared firm-scope-db-pins corpus exactly. No applied migration was edited, no PRD/ARCHITECTURE edit, no frozen-workflow manifest diff, and the one frozen file this lane's #975 successor contract depends on (depreciation-run.ts) is confirmed untouched. Re-running the claimed test batteries (62/62 db focused files, 33 operation-census/rig-isolation with the one known T19 skip, 20/20 runtime, 47/47 web unit files touched) reproduced every count the four ticket reports claim exactly, and typecheck/CI-mode lint are both clean. TDD vertical slicing was followed at the commit level throughout, with one deliberate, reported, and rule-4-compensated exception in #975. Two minor findings survive review, both judgement calls rather than hard violations: a small Duplicated Code smell (completeIntent re-implements reviseIntent's particulars-serialisation logic verbatim in the same file) and a test-naming precision nit (a disposeIntent test title claims a runtime-verified 'memo EXCLUDED' behaviour that is actually enforced by the type system and only documented, not asserted, in the test body). Nothing found rises to a documented-standard violation.
